The proof is rearrangement-free and relies on a critical Hardy inequality with remainder, scale-invariant Sobolev inequalities, and a refined dyadic summation argument.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to strengthen existing quantitative stability estimates for the critical Hardy inequality, which previously had suboptimal dependence on the distance function (exponent N²) and relied on more complex frameworks (Lorentz-Zygmund spaces) and artificial cut-off modifications of extremizers.
AI.method: The proof is completely rearrangement-free and uses three key ingredients: (1) a critical Hardy inequality with a remainder term, (2) scale-invariant Sobolev inequalities, and (3) a refined dyadic summation argument. The stability is measured in the Luxemburg norm of the critical exponential Orlicz space ExpL^{N/(N-1)}(Ω), replacing the earlier Lorentz-Zygmund framework. The distance to virtual extremizers is measured directly without truncation.
AI.result: The exponent in the distance function is reduced from N² to N for both the standard critical Hardy inequality and the logarithmic-weight variant due to Cianchi and Ferone. The new estimates hold in the critical exponential Orlicz space without requiring any cut-off modification of virtual extremizers, yielding stronger quantitative stability results in both cases.
AI.conclusion: The authors obtain optimal or near-optimal quantitative stability estimates for the critical Hardy inequality, improving both the exponent and the functional framework compared to prior results. The rearrangement-free proof strategy is general enough to apply to both the standard and logarithmically weighted formulations of the critical Hardy inequality.

title: Second-Order Continuum Model for Disordered Traffic
comment: 44 pages, submitted to Transp. Res. Part B
summary: In this study, a two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model is proposed to capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic by explicitly incorporating coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions. The framework extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions and introduces acceleration equations consisting of self-driven, interaction-induced, and road-boundary-related components. The macroscopic longitudinal acceleration is formulated based on the Full Velocity Difference Model (FVDM), while lateral dynamics are governed by interaction principles consistent with the Optimal Velocity Model (OVM). The explicit inclusion of road-boundary effects enables the representation of vehicle confinement and space-sharing behavior that are essential in lane-free and weakly lane-disciplined traffic systems. The model is examined through a series of numerical experiments in which longitudinal and lateral dynamics are analysed individually as well as simultaneously within a coupled two-dimensional setting under a range of initial conditions, including transitions between free-flow, medium congestion, and heavy congestion, and different lateral density configurations. The simulations demonstrate the model's ability to reproduce key traffic features such as shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across the road width. The numerical scheme, based on upwind and Lax-Friedrichs discretisations, ensures stable solutions of the coupled partial differential equations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust macroscopic description of disordered traffic and offers a consistent basis for analysing two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics.

AI.tldr: A two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model is proposed that couples longitudinal and lateral interactions, extends the continuity equation to 2D, and incorporates road-boundary effects to capture disordered traffic dynamics like shockwaves, lateral dispersion, and vehicle rearrangement in lane-free traffic systems.
AI.motivation: To capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic—particularly in lane-free and weakly lane-disciplined systems—where traditional one-dimensional models cannot represent coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions, vehicle confinement, and space-sharing behavior.
AI.method: Extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions with acceleration equations comprising self-driven, interaction-induced, and road-boundary-related components. Longitudinal acceleration is based on the Full Velocity Difference Model (FVDM), lateral dynamics follow the Optimal Velocity Model (OVM), and the numerical scheme uses upwind and Lax-Friedrichs discretisations.
AI.result: Numerical experiments under various initial conditions (free-flow, medium/heavy congestion, different lateral density configurations) demonstrate the model reproduces shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across road width. The numerical scheme ensures stable solutions of the coupled PDEs.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a robust macroscopic description of disordered traffic and offers a consistent basis for analysing two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics.

title: On symmetric systems of transport equations
summary: We study a symmetric system of transport equations with solenoidal coefficients. This system reduces to an evolutionary equation with a skew-symmetric spatial operator in the real Hilbert space of square-integrable vector-functions, and by general results we claim that there always exists a generalized solution of the Cauchy problem. Uniqueness of this solution is equivalent to skew-adjointness of the spatial operator. We demonstrate that in the case of locally Lipschitz coefficients satisfying a linear growth condition the spatial transport operator is indeed skew-adjoint. For scalar transport equation this result remains true under the weaker DiPerna-Lions conditions.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes a symmetric system of transport equations with solenoidal coefficients, proving the existence of generalized solutions to the Cauchy problem via the skew-symmetry of the spatial operator, and establishing skew-adjointness under different regularity conditions (locally Lipschitz with linear growth for systems, DiPerna-Lions conditions for scalar equations), which guarantees uniqueness.
AI.motivation: To establish well-posedness (existence and uniqueness) of generalized solutions for symmetric transport equations with solenoidal coefficients, by linking uniqueness to the skew-adjointness of the associated spatial operator.
AI.method: The system is reformulated as an evolutionary equation with a skew-symmetric spatial operator in L² space. Existence follows from general abstract results. Uniqueness is shown to be equivalent to skew-adjointness of the spatial operator, which is then verified under locally Lipschitz coefficients with linear growth, and under the weaker DiPerna-Lions conditions in the scalar case.
AI.result: The spatial transport operator is proven to be skew-adjoint for locally Lipschitz coefficients satisfying a linear growth condition, yielding uniqueness. For scalar transport equations, the skew-adjointness result holds under the weaker DiPerna-Lions regularity conditions.
AI.conclusion: The symmetric transport system admits a unique generalized solution of the Cauchy problem under the stated coefficient regularity conditions, as existence is guaranteed by general theory and uniqueness follows from the established skew-adjointness of the spatial operator.

title: Efficient Classical Simulation of Weakly Interacting Fermion Dynamics
summary: We consider the task of simulating the real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems. In particular, we focus on computing the expectation value of a local observable $A$ at time $t$. By analyzing the convergence of the perturbative expansion in the interaction strength $λ$ for the Heisenberg-picture observable, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for estimating this expectation value in the weakly interacting regime $λ|t|^{2D+1}=\mathcal{O}(1)$, when the Hamiltonian is geometrically local on a $D$-dimensional lattice. Importantly, this condition is independent of the system size. If the goal is instead to approximate the time-evolved observable in normalized Frobenius norm, we extend the convergence regime to $λ|t|=\mathcal{O}(1)$ with quasi-polynomial runtime. When the non-interacting part exhibits Anderson localization, our polynomial-time algorithm can be extended up to $λ|t|=\mathcal{O}(1)$, modulo polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm brings together ideas from continuous-time QMC, diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana Propagation, but with a new Heisenberg-picture operator-growth analysis that makes the sampling complexity rigorously controllable. This leads to provably efficient classical algorithms in regimes where the interaction is weak enough that the sampling variance remains bounded independently of system size. Together, these results identify broad regimes in which weak interactions, locality, and localization can be leveraged to make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes polynomial-time classical algorithms for simulating real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems on D-dimensional lattices, using a Heisenberg-picture perturbative expansion with rigorously controlled sampling complexity. The algorithm works when λ|t|^{2D+1}=O(1) for local observables (system-size independent), extends to λ|t|=O(1) with quasi-polynomial runtime for Frobenius norm approximation, and can be improved to λ|t|=O(1) modulo polylog factors under Anderson localization.
AI.motivation: Simulating real-time dynamics of interacting quantum systems is generally classically intractable, yet many physically relevant fermionic systems have weak interactions. The authors aim to identify provably efficient classical algorithms for such weakly interacting regimes, leveraging locality and the structure of perturbative expansions to go beyond what brute-force simulation allows.
AI.method: The algorithm combines ideas from continuous-time Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana Propagation. The key novelty is a Heisenberg-picture operator-growth analysis that makes the sampling complexity rigorously controllable. The approach analyzes convergence of the perturbative expansion in interaction strength λ for the Heisenberg-picture observable, showing that weak couplings allow efficient classical estimation.
AI.result: The algorithm achieves polynomial-time estimation of local observable expectation values when λ|t|^{2D+1}=O(1) (system-size independent) for geometrically local Hamiltonians. For normalized Frobenius norm approximation of the time-evolved observable, the convergence regime extends to λ|t|=O(1) with quasi-polynomial runtime. Under Anderson localization, polynomial-time scaling holds up to λ|t|=O(1) modulo polylogarithmic factors.
AI.conclusion: The results identify broad regimes where weak interactions, locality, and localization can be exploited to make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable with provable guarantees, bridging concepts across QMC methods while providing rigorous complexity bounds.

title: Weighted Perimeters and pth Moments of Inertia of Convex Curves and Surfaces
summary: We study a shape optimization problem among convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ that minimize or maximize weighted perimeters of the form $\int_{\partialΩ} φ(|x|) \, \mathrm{d} H^{n-1}(x)$ under a standard perimeter constraint. We prove the existence of extremals for general weight functions in any dimension. In dimension two, we prove that the degenerate needle configuration $(-a,a)\times \{0\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is the optimizer for a wide family of weights, including $|x|^p$ for $p \in (0,2]$ and $|x|^{-α}$ for $α\in (0,1)$, among convex curves satisfying a symmetry assumption.

AI.tldr: The paper studies shape optimization among convex bodies in R^n, seeking minimizers/maximizers of weighted perimeters ∫∂Ω φ(|x|) dH^{n-1} under a standard perimeter constraint. Existence of extremals is proven for general weights in any dimension, and in 2D the degenerate needle configuration is shown to be optimal for a wide family of weights under symmetry assumptions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how anisotropic or radially weighted perimeter functionals behave under optimization over convex bodies, extending classical isoperimetric-type questions to weighted settings where extremal shapes may degenerate.
AI.method: The approach combines existence theory for shape optimization problems with convex bodies in arbitrary dimension, and in dimension two, a targeted analysis showing that the degenerate needle configuration (-a,a)×{0} serves as the optimizer for a broad family of weight functions (including |x|^p for p∈(0,2] and |x|^{-α} for α∈(0,1)) among convex curves satisfying a symmetry assumption.
AI.result: Existence of extremals is established for general weight functions in any dimension. In dimension two, the degenerate needle configuration is proven to be the optimizer for a wide family of weights, including polynomial and inverse-power weights, under a symmetry condition.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes both a general existence result for weighted perimeter optimization over convex bodies and identifies the degenerate needle as the shape-optimal configuration in 2D for a substantial class of weight functions under symmetry constraints.

title: Beyond linear subspaces: Nonlinear moment matching meets quadratic manifolds
summary: Quadratic manifold-based model order reduction offers a viable pathway to circumvent the limitations of linear subspaces for linear control systems characterized by slow Kolmogorov $n$-width decay. However, a system-theoretic framework for constructing such quadratic approximations remains absent from the literature. This paper presents a system-agnostic, optimization-free framework for the direct construction of quadratic projection matrices. We prove that the synthesized reduced-order model matches the nonlinear moments of the full-order system and preserves its exact center manifold mapping, thereby ensuring asymptotic tracking of steady-state outputs under specific input classes. Numerical results on transport-dominated benchmark problems, namely, the one-dimensional damped wave and advection equations, show that the proposed framework achieves high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction within a significantly reduced-dimensional state space, yielding substantial online computational savings.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a system-agnostic, optimization-free framework for directly constructing quadratic projection matrices for model order reduction of linear control systems with slow Kolmogorov n-width decay, proving the reduced-order model matches nonlinear moments and preserves the center manifold mapping.
AI.motivation: Linear subspace-based model order reduction fails for systems characterized by slow Kolmogorov n-width decay, and quadratic manifold-based approaches exist but lack a system-theoretic framework for constructing the quadratic approximations.
AI.method: A system-agnostic, optimization-free framework for direct construction of quadratic projection matrices, with proven matching of nonlinear moments and preservation of the exact center manifold mapping of the full-order system.
AI.result: On transport-dominated benchmarks (1D damped wave and advection equations), the framework achieves high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction in a significantly reduced-dimensional state space with substantial online computational savings.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework enables effective quadratic manifold-based model reduction with theoretical guarantees on moment matching and asymptotic tracking of steady-state outputs, providing a system-theoretic foundation previously missing from the literature.

title: On the Local boundedness and higher integrability for the subcritical doubly nonlinear parabolic systems
summary: We consider the inhomogeneous doubly nonlinear parabolic systems of the form \begin{equation*}\partial_t (|u|^{q-1}u)-\operatorname{div}(|Du|^{p-2}Du)=\operatorname{div}(|F|^{p-2}F)\end{equation*} in a bounded space-time cylinder $Ω_T=Ω\times(0,T)\subset \mathbb{R}^{N+1}$. We study the local regularity properties for weak solutions in the subcritical range $p\leq\frac{N(q+1)}{N+q+1}$ and $0<q<\frac{N+2}{N-2}$. Under an extra integrability assumption $|u|\in L_{\loc}^{\rr}(Ω_T)$, we establish a quantitative bound for $|u|$. Here, the exponent $\rr$ satisfies $\mathrmλ_{\rr}=N(p-q-1)+p\rr>0$. In addition, we prove local higher integrability of $|Du|$ in the range $p=\frac{N(q+1)}{N+q+1}$ and $\frac{N+p}{N-p}<q<\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, provided that $|u|\in L_{\loc}^{\rr}(Ω_T)$ holds.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes local regularity properties for weak solutions of inhomogeneous doubly nonlinear parabolic systems in the subcritical range, proving a quantitative bound on |u| under an extra integrability assumption and local higher integrability of |Du| in a specific critical-range case.
AI.motivation: To extend the understanding of regularity for weak solutions to doubly nonlinear parabolic systems, particularly in the subcritical range where p ≤ N(q+1)/(N+q+1), which has received less attention than other parameter regimes.
AI.method: The authors consider the inhomogeneous doubly nonlinear parabolic system and impose the subcritical condition p ≤ N(q+1)/(N+q+1) with 0 < q < (N+2)/(N-2). They assume an extra integrability condition |u| ∈ L^r_loc(Ω_T) with the exponent satisfying λ_r = N(p-q-1) + pr > 0, and derive a quantitative bound for |u|. For the critical case p = N(q+1)/(N+q+1) with (N+p)/(N-p) < q < (N+2)/(N-2), they additionally prove local higher integrability of |Du|.
AI.result: A quantitative bound for the solution |u| is established under the stated integrability assumption in the subcritical range. Furthermore, local higher integrability of |Du| is proven in the case p = N(q+1)/(N+q+1) with (N+p)/(N-p) < q < (N+2)/(N-2), again under the same extra integrability assumption on |u|.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides new regularity results for inhomogeneous doubly nonlinear parabolic systems in the subcritical parameter range, showing that an extra integrability assumption on the solution enables quantitative bounds and higher integrability of the gradient.

title: Rationally Enriched Chebyshev Trunk Bases for DeepONet Surrogates of High Péclet Entrance Transport
summary: This study demonstrates a rationally enriched Chebyshev (REC) trunk for deep operator network (DeepONet) surrogate models of singularly perturbed and high-Péclet transport problems whose solution profiles are characterized by thin localized boundary or wall layers. The REC trunk combines Chebyshev polynomial dictionary elements with rational dictionary elements constructed using the adaptive Antoulas-Anderson (AAA) algorithm. Over five independent training runs, the resulting REC-trunk DeepONet is evaluated against a vanilla DeepONet and a Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet whose prescribed dictionary consists only of Chebyshev polynomials across three problems whose singular perturbation parameters are diffusion-to-advection ratios: a singularly perturbed scalar boundary-value problem (BVP), the thermal entrance problem with a prescribed wall temperature, and the concentration entrance problem with an absorbing wall. Across the held-out test profiles, the REC-trunk DeepONet improves over the vanilla DeepONet and remains comparable to the Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet in predicting the scalar profile, with its clearest advantage over the Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet appearing when the perturbation parameter lies between $1.00\times10^{-4}$ and $1.78\times10^{-4}$, where it reduces the profile-error metrics by up to $19.5\,\%$ relative to the Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet. In predicting the wall-normal temperature and concentration profiles, the REC-trunk DeepONet reduces the profile-error metrics by up to $60.2\,\%$ and $32.2\,\%$ relative to the vanilla and Chebyshev-trunk DeepONets, respectively, while suppressing artificial near-wall oscillations as the Péclet or mass-transfer Péclet number ranges from $10^{2}$ to $10^{4}$.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a rationally enriched Chebyshev (REC) trunk for DeepONet surrogate models targeting transport problems with thin boundary/wall layers. The REC trunk combines Chebyshev polynomials with rational functions from the AAA algorithm, and is shown to outperform both vanilla and Chebyshev-only DeepONets—reducing profile errors by up to 19.5% (vs Chebyshev), 60.2% (vs vanilla), and 32.2% (vs Chebyshev) while suppressing artificial near-wall oscillations across three test problems.
AI.motivation: Solutions to singularly perturbed and high-Péclet transport problems feature thin localized boundary or wall layers that are difficult for standard neural-network surrogates to resolve. Vanilla DeepONets and even Chebyshev-polynomial-trunk DeepONets struggle to capture these sharp layer profiles accurately and without spurious oscillations, motivating a trunk design that better matches the rational-like structure of these solutions.
AI.method: The REC trunk enriches Chebyshev polynomial basis functions with rational dictionary elements generated by the adaptive Antoulas-Anderson (AAA) algorithm. This hybrid dictionary is used as the trunk in a DeepONet, and the model is trained with five independent runs and evaluated on three benchmark problems with varying singular perturbation parameters (diffusion-to-advection ratios): a singularly perturbed scalar BVP, a thermal entrance problem, and a concentration entrance problem.
AI.result: The REC-trunk DeepONet outperforms the vanilla DeepONet and is comparable to the Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet for scalar profiles, with the clearest gains (up to 19.5% error reduction) at perturbation parameters in [1.00e-4, 1.78e-4]. For wall-normal temperature and concentration profiles, it reduces errors by up to 60.2% vs the vanilla and 32.2% vs the Chebyshev-trunk DeepONet, while eliminating artificial near-wall oscillations for Péclet/mass-transfer Péclet numbers from 1e2 to 1e4.
AI.conclusion: The REC trunk offers a practical improvement for DeepONet surrogates in layer-dominated transport problems, especially for wall-normal profiles where rational enrichment suppresses oscillations and improves accuracy. The approach is most advantageous in the intermediate perturbation-parameter regime and holds promise for robust surrogate modeling of stiff/boundary-layer physics.

title: Energy rigidity and weak-strong uniqueness for the 2D anisotropic Navier-Stokes equations
summary: In two dimensions, we show that dissipation in one spatial direction is sufficient to enforce the energy equality for every weak solution at the natural energy level. In particular, neither anomalous energy loss nor creation can occur. The main difficulty is that the missing directional regularity prevents the usual self-testing argument. We overcome this obstruction through two observations: The pressure is square-integrable by a directional Riesz-transform estimate, and the less regular component is still a renormalized solution. As an application of energy rigidity, we derive a weak-strong uniqueness principle.

AI.tldr: In 2D, dissipation in just one spatial direction suffices to enforce the energy equality for all weak solutions at the natural energy level, preventing anomalous energy loss or creation. This is achieved by overcoming the missing directional regularity via two key observations: square-integrability of pressure from a directional Riesz-transform estimate, and the less regular component being a renormalized solution.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses whether partial (one-directional) dissipation is sufficient to guarantee energy conservation for weak solutions in 2D fluid dynamics, eliminating the possibility of anomalous energy behavior (loss or creation).
AI.method: The authors overcome the obstruction of missing directional regularity (which prevents the standard self-testing/energy equality argument) through two observations: (1) proving the pressure is square-integrable via a directional Riesz-transform estimate, and (2) showing the less regular velocity component is still a renormalized solution.
AI.result: They prove that one-directional dissipation enforces the energy equality for every weak solution at the natural energy level in 2D. As an application, they derive a weak-strong uniqueness principle from this energy rigidity.
AI.conclusion: Dissipation in a single spatial direction is sufficient to rule out anomalous energy behavior in 2D, and this energy rigidity can be leveraged to establish weak-strong uniqueness.

title: Learning piecewise-smooth dynamical systems
summary: Discovering dynamical systems from trajectory data is a central problem in applied mathematics and engineering. Whilst recent advances in machine learning have led to strong progress in data-driven system identification, much less attention has been given to systems with discontinuous dynamics. These systems are nevertheless highly relevant in applications, including climate dynamics and mechanical systems with friction. In this work, we consider the problem of identifying piecewise-smooth dynamical systems directly from trajectory data. Compared with the smooth setting, this requires recovering the governing equations and detecting the switching hyperplanes that separate different dynamical regimes and characterising their behaviour, such as sliding motion. We present a modular framework for discovering such systems by first estimating switching hyperplanes from data and then learning smooth dynamics within each region using geometry-constrained neural networks. The geometry-learning phase is studied from a statistical perspective, analysing the identifiability of the discontinuities and the robustness of the procedure. We also introduce a novel neural network architecture with a prescribed discontinuity set, and provide a theoretical analysis of its approximation properties. The approach is tested on low-dimensional benchmark problems, including dry-friction oscillators and the PP04 climate model for the ice ages.

AI.tldr: A modular framework for discovering piecewise-smooth dynamical systems from trajectory data, combining switching hyperplane detection with geometry-constrained neural networks, tested on low-dimensional benchmarks including friction oscillators and climate models.
AI.motivation: While machine learning has advanced data-driven system identification for smooth dynamical systems, much less attention has been given to systems with discontinuous dynamics, which are highly relevant in applications like climate dynamics and mechanical systems with friction.
AI.method: A modular framework with two stages: (1) estimating switching hyperplanes from trajectory data to segment different dynamical regimes, and (2) learning smooth dynamics within each region using geometry-constrained neural networks. A novel neural network architecture with a prescribed discontinuity set is introduced, with theoretical approximation analysis and statistical treatment of identifiability and robustness.
AI.result: The approach is validated on low-dimensional benchmark problems, including dry-friction oscillators and the PP04 climate model for ice ages, demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in recovering governing equations and detecting switching hyperplanes with sliding motion characterization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a principled approach to discovering piecewise-smooth dynamical systems by combining hyperplane estimation with geometry-constrained neural networks, with theoretical guarantees on identifiability and approximation properties.

title: Classification of global solutions to the singular equation $-Δu=f(X)\cdot u^{-γ}$ in a Lipschitz epigraphical cone
summary:
We construct and classify all global solutions to the singular equation $$-Δu=f(X)\cdot u^{-γ}$$ supported in a general Lipschitz epigraphical cone, where $f(X)$ is a locally Dini continuous function with $0<λ\leq f(X)\leqΛ$. The existence and non-existence of a global solution is solely determined by the exponent $γ$ of the equation and the ``frequency" of the cone.
  Moreover, in order to classify all global solutions, we introduce several new methods. First, we use the local data to estimate the global growth rate, which in turn establishes the boundedness of the ``asymptotic slope" of the global solution. Second, by establishing a nonlinear variant of Kemper's boundary Harnack principle, we classify all global solutions through an ``oscillation reduction" argument on the ``asymptotic slope".

AI.tldr: This paper classifies all global solutions to the singular elliptic equation -Δu = f(X)·u^{-γ} in a Lipschitz epigraphical cone, showing that existence and uniqueness of global solutions depends on the exponent γ and the cone's "frequency."
AI.motivation: To fully characterize the structure of global solutions to singular boundary value problems in general Lipschitz epigraphical cones, which is fundamental for understanding their asymptotic behavior and classification.
AI.method: Two new techniques are introduced: (1) using local data to estimate the global growth rate, establishing boundedness of the "asymptotic slope" of global solutions; (2) establishing a nonlinear variant of Kemper's boundary Harnack principle to classify all global solutions via an "oscillation reduction" argument on the asymptotic slope.
AI.result: The existence and non-existence of global solutions is solely determined by the exponent γ and the "frequency" of the cone, and all global solutions are fully classified.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a complete classification of global solutions to the singular equation in general Lipschitz epigraphical cones, extending prior results through novel analytic techniques.

title: Applying the Spectral Method for Modeling Linear Filters: Bessel, Papoulis, and Legendre Filters
summary: This paper proposes a new technique for computer simulation of linear filters. It allows simulating continuous-time linear filters based on the spectral method for analyzing linear control systems. Applying the spectral method implies that the input and output signals are represented by ordered sets of expansion coefficients in a chosen basis, and the filter itself is specified by a two-dimensional nonstationary transfer function. The described technique is tested on Bessel, Papoulis, and Legendre filters of various orders. For each filter, the corresponding two-dimensional nonstationary transfer function, i.e., the matrix of the linear transformation relating expansion coefficients of the input and output signals, is obtained.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new technique for simulating continuous-time linear filters using a spectral method, where signals are represented by expansion coefficients in a chosen basis and filters are described by two-dimensional nonstationary transfer function matrices. The method is tested on Bessel, Papoulis, and Legendre filters of various orders.
AI.motivation: To develop an improved technique for computer simulation of continuous-time linear filters that leverages the spectral method for analyzing linear control systems, offering an alternative to traditional time-domain simulation approaches.
AI.method: The technique applies the spectral method, representing input and output signals as ordered sets of expansion coefficients in a chosen basis. The filter is specified as a two-dimensional nonstationary transfer function—a matrix that linearly transforms input expansion coefficients into output expansion coefficients.
AI.result: The technique was successfully tested on Bessel, Papoulis, and Legendre filters of various orders, and for each filter, the corresponding two-dimensional nonstationary transfer function (transformation matrix) was obtained.
AI.conclusion: The proposed spectral-based simulation technique is effective for continuous-time linear filters, successfully producing nonstationary transfer function matrices for several classical filter types.

title: Weakly stable solutions of Serrin's problem
summary: We prove that weakly stable solutions of Serrin's problem are compact and therefore round balls.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that weakly stable solutions of Serrin's problem are compact and thus must be round balls.
AI.motivation: Serrin's problem concerns overdetermined boundary value problems, and establishing that weakly stable solutions are compact and round balls is a fundamental rigidity result in the theory of elliptic PDEs and free boundary problems.
AI.method: The proof establishes compactness of weakly stable solutions and then shows that compactness implies the domain must be a round ball.
AI.result: Weakly stable solutions of Serrin's problem are proven to be compact, and consequently they are round balls.
AI.conclusion: The rigidity result confirms that under weak stability, the only possible solutions to Serrin's problem are round balls, extending the classical understanding of this problem.

title: Mean curvature bounds for the obstacle problem
summary: We prove optimal $(n-1)$-semiconvexity estimates for solutions to the classical obstacle problem, possibly with a smooth right-hand side. We deduce that the mean curvature of the free boundary is universally bounded above in all dimensions. Existing examples show that full curvature bounds fail in dimensions three and higher. Noticeably, these results are novel even for a constant right-hand side in the $n=2$ case.

AI.tldr: This paper proves optimal (n-1)-semiconvexity estimates for solutions to the classical obstacle problem with a smooth right-hand side, and consequently shows that the mean curvature of the free boundary is universally bounded above in all dimensions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to establish optimal semiconvexity estimates for the obstacle problem and bound the mean curvature of the free boundary, addressing a gap where full curvature bounds are known to fail in dimensions three and higher, making the results novel even in the 2D constant right-hand side case.
AI.method: The paper proves optimal (n-1)-semiconvexity estimates for solutions to the classical obstacle problem, possibly including a smooth right-hand side, using analytical techniques tailored to the obstacle problem structure.
AI.result: The authors obtain optimal (n-1)-semiconvexity estimates and deduce a universal upper bound on the mean curvature of the free boundary in all dimensions. These results are novel even for n=2 with a constant right-hand side.
AI.conclusion: The results establish sharp semiconvexity estimates and mean curvature bounds for the free boundary, complementing existing examples that show full curvature bounds fail in dimensions three and higher.

title: On a visco-elastic Mullins-Sekerka System
summary: We introduce a novel visco-elastic Mullins-Sekerka system with a prescribed constant contact angle at the boundary. The system is derived as an $H^{-1}$-$H^1$-type gradient flow of an energy consisting of the perimeter together with capillary, elastic, and second-gradient contributions. Building on the framework of Hensel and Stinson (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 248, 2024), we introduce a measure-valued solution concept featuring a sharp De Giorgi-type energy-dissipation inequality. Moreover, we establish existence of solutions via an implicit time discretization scheme, and prove existence of $BV$ solutions under an energy-conservation hypothesis.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a visco-elastic Mullins-Sekerka system with constant contact angle boundary conditions, derived as an H^-1-H^1 gradient flow of an energy combining perimeter, capillary, elastic, and second-gradient terms. Building on Hensel and Stinson's framework, it develops a measure-valued solution concept with a De Giorgi-type energy-dissipation inequality, proves existence via implicit time discretization, and establishes BV solutions under an energy-conservation hypothesis.
AI.motivation: To extend the Mullins-Sekerka system to incorporate visco-elastic effects with prescribed contact angle boundary conditions, building on prior work by Hensel and Stinson to develop a rigorous analytical framework for this more general physical setting.
AI.method: The system is formulated as an H^-1-H^1 gradient flow of an energy functional containing perimeter, capillary, elastic, and second-gradient terms. Solutions are defined in a measure-valued sense with a De Giorgi-type energy-dissipation inequality, and existence is established through implicit time discretization (minimizing movements) techniques.
AI.result: Existence of solutions is established via the implicit time discretization scheme. Additionally, existence of BV solutions is proven under an energy-conservation hypothesis.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous analytical foundation for the visco-elastic Mullins-Sekerka system with constant contact angle, establishing existence results within a measure-valued solution framework and identifying conditions under which more regular BV solutions exist.

title: Stability of admissible solutions for coexisting phase transitions for one-dimensional compressible van der Waals fluids
summary: In this paper, we investigate the dynamic stability of certain steady-state solutions to the periodic boundary value problem for compressible isentropic Navier-Stokes system under the van der Waals equation of state in one space dimension. These steady-state solutions correspond to the admissible solutions describing two-phase coexisting phase transitions, where the integral average of the specific volume belongs to the Maxwell region. We first construct a semi-discrete staggered grid difference scheme to prove the local existence of solutions to the periodic problem, without imposing the standard stability hypothesis \(p_v<0\). Then, by virtue of rigorous piecewise a priori estimates, we demonstrate that the periodic boundary value problem for van der Waals fluids possesses a global solution existing for all time, and this solution converges uniformly to the admissible steady state as time tends to infinity. This result firmly establishes the nonlinear stability of the admissible phase-transition solutions under general small initial disturbances.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the nonlinear dynamic stability of admissible two-phase steady-state solutions to the periodic boundary value problem for the compressible isentropic Navier-Stokes system with van der Waals equation of state in 1D. Without assuming the standard stability hypothesis p_v<0, the authors construct a semi-discrete staggered grid difference scheme for local existence and derive rigorous piecewise a priori estimates to establish global existence and uniform convergence to the admissible steady state.
AI.motivation: To establish the nonlinear stability of admissible phase-transition solutions for van der Waals fluids without relying on the standard stability hypothesis p_v<0, which is not satisfied in the Maxwell region where two-phase coexistence occurs.
AI.method: (1) Construct a semi-discrete staggered grid difference scheme to prove local existence of solutions for the periodic problem without the standard stability hypothesis; (2) Use rigorous piecewise a priori estimates to demonstrate global existence; (3) Show uniform convergence of the solution to the admissible steady state as time tends to infinity.
AI.result: The periodic boundary value problem for van der Waals fluids possesses a global solution for all time, and this solution converges uniformly to the admissible steady state as time tends to infinity, establishing nonlinear stability under general small initial disturbances.
AI.conclusion: The nonlinear stability of admissible phase-transition solutions for the compressible isentropic Navier-Stokes system with van der Waals equation of state is firmly established under general small initial disturbances, without requiring the standard stability hypothesis p_v<0.

title: Flexibility for the Three-Dimensional Navier-Stokes Equations via Moving Hill Vortices
summary:
We construct weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus. The convex-integration scheme is based on the moving-dipole construction of Bruè, Colombo, and Kumar~\cite{BrueColomboKumar2024}. For the explicit exponent $\bar p=\frac65+5\times10^{-5},$ and for any two mean-zero, divergence-free vector fields in $L^2(\mathbb T^3)$, we construct a weak solution whose traces at times $0$ and $1$ approximate the prescribed fields arbitrarily well and which satisfies
  \[
  u\in C([0,1];L^2(\mathbb T^3)),
  \qquad
  \nabla u\in C([0,1];L^{\bar p}(\mathbb T^3)).
  \] Exploiting the time-locality of the iteration, we also obtain exact nonuniqueness for a dense set of initial data in \(L^2_σ(\mathbb T^3)\).The principal perturbations are localized, rescaled copies of Hill's spherical vortex. The Hill scaling preserves both the kinetic-energy scale and the \(L^{6/5}\)-scale of the velocity gradient. The construction uses localization of the potential exterior flow, long-orbit averaging of moving vortex cores, an auxiliary source correction, and a temporal corrector compatible with uniform-in-time Sobolev control.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs weak solutions to the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus using a convex-integration scheme based on moving dipoles. The solutions are continuous in L² and have gradients in L^{6/5+5×10⁻⁵}, achieving arbitrary approximation of prescribed initial/final data and exact nonuniqueness for a dense set of initial data in L²_σ.
AI.motivation: To construct weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with enhanced regularity properties beyond previously known results, improving the exponent for the velocity gradient to reach p̄ = 6/5 + 5×10⁻⁵, and to establish nonuniqueness for a dense set of initial data.
AI.method: A convex-integration scheme built on the moving-dipole construction of Bruè, Colombo, and Kumar. Key components include: (1) localized rescaled Hill's spherical vortices preserving both kinetic-energy and L^{6/5}-gradient scales, (2) localization of potential exterior flow, (3) long-orbit averaging of moving vortex cores, (4) an auxiliary source correction, and (5) a temporal corrector ensuring uniform-in-time Sobolev control.
AI.result: Weak solutions u ∈ C([0,1];L²(T³)) with ∇u ∈ C([0,1];L^{p̄}(T³)) for p̄ = 6/5 + 5×10⁻⁵ are constructed, approximating arbitrary mean-zero divergence-free L² fields at times 0 and 1. Exact nonuniqueness is obtained for a dense set of initial data in L²_σ(T³).
AI.conclusion: The time-local nature of the iteration enables stronger nonuniqueness results than previous approaches, and the Hill vortex-based perturbations achieve finer regularity thresholds (exponent above 6/5) than earlier convex-integration schemes for Navier-Stokes.

title: Calderón-Zygmund estimates for parabolic systems with $p$-growth and non-divergence data
summary: We obtain Calderón--Zygmund estimates for weak solutions to nonlinear parabolic systems with polynomial $p$-growth and the right-hand side in non-divergence form. Our approach does not require differentiability of the vector field with respect to the gradient variable and provides a unified treatment of both the singular and degenerate regimes. In particular, we establish local higher-integrability estimates for the gradient of the solution under appropriate dependency on the integrability of the right-hand side.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes Calderón-Zygmund estimates for weak solutions to nonlinear parabolic systems with polynomial p-growth, where the right-hand side is in non-divergence form. The approach avoids differentiability assumptions on the vector field with respect to the gradient and unifies treatment of singular and degenerate regimes, yielding local higher-integrability estimates for the gradient.
AI.motivation: To obtain Calderón-Zygmund (higher-integrability) estimates for weak solutions of nonlinear parabolic systems with p-growth in the non-divergence case, extending existing results that typically require differentiability of the vector field and separate treatment of singular versus degenerate regimes.
AI.method: A unified approach that does not require differentiability of the vector field with respect to the gradient variable, treating both the singular (p<2) and degenerate (p≥2) regimes simultaneously in the non-divergence setting.
AI.result: Local higher-integrability estimates for the gradient of weak solutions are established, with dependence on the integrability of the right-hand side.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides unified Calderón-Zygmund estimates for nonlinear parabolic systems with p-growth and non-divergence right-hand sides, removing the differentiability assumption on the vector field and covering both singular and degenerate cases.

title: Scattering for the focusing $H^{1/2}$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation with large data
summary:
In this article we prove that the solution to the focusing $H^{1/2}$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in dimension $d\geq 5$ scatters outside finitely many arbitrarily small spacetime cones. We will discuss the relationship between Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-bad-directions} and the resolution of solitons. There are two key ingredients in the proof: the localized below-ground-state scattering in Theorem~\ref{thm:cone-scattering}, and the characterization in Theorem~\ref{thm:measure-convergence} of the asymptotic behaviour of the residual part (i.e., after subtracting the scattering part).
  As a byproduct, we also establish an upgrading machinery: if the solution is below the ground state (resp. small) along a time sequence in a spacetime cone, then it is also below ground state (resp. small) uniformly for large time in a shrinked spacetime cone. We expect this to be useful in future works using concentration compactness and our spacetime cone approach.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that solutions to the focusing H^{1/2}-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in dimension d≥5 scatter outside finitely many arbitrarily small spacetime cones. The proof relies on two key ingredients: localized below-ground-state scattering and a characterization of the asymptotic behavior of the residual part. The paper also establishes an upgrading machinery showing that if a solution is below ground state along a time sequence in a spacetime cone, it remains so uniformly for large times in a shrinked cone.
AI.motivation: To understand the long-time behavior of solutions to the focusing H^{1/2}-critical NLS equation in high dimensions, specifically to determine scattering behavior outside a finite set of "bad directions" and relate this to the resolution of solitons conjecture.
AI.method: The proof combines two key ingredients: (1) a localized below-ground-state scattering theorem for spacetime cones, and (2) a characterization theorem of the asymptotic behavior of the residual part (the part obtained after subtracting the scattering component). Additionally, an upgrading machinery is established that converts below-ground-state (or smallness) conditions along a time sequence in a cone to uniform conditions in a shrinked cone for large times.
AI.result: The main result establishes scattering outside finitely many arbitrarily small spacetime cones for the focusing H^{1/2}-critical NLS in dimension d≥5. As a byproduct, the upgrading machinery is proven, which is expected to be useful in future concentration compactness approaches combined with the spacetime cone method.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a new scattering result for the critical NLS equation that constrains scattering failure to finitely many small spacetime cones, and offers a tool (upgrading machinery) for future work connecting concentration compactness with spacetime cone techniques.

title: Backstepping-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Wide-Range Saint-Venant Canal Regulation
summary: Backstepping control provides local stability guarantees for nonlinear Saint-Venant systems, but its regulation performance may degrade when the system operates far from the nominal equilibrium. This letter proposes a backstepping-guided soft actor-critic (SAC) controller framework that incorporates model-based control knowledge into reinforcement learning (RL). The nominal backstepping control law is first learned by deep operator network (DeepONet) and embedded into the actor and critic networks as prior informed feature representations. The learned prior is further combined with the SAC policy to generate the final control input, while a transfer-learning strategy preserves the useful backstepping knowledge during adaptation to the nonlinear dynamics. Simulation results on the Sambre River model demonstrate that the proposed method improves learning efficiency and maintains effective regulation over larger initial deviations than backstepping control.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a backstepping-guided soft actor-critic (SAC) framework for nonlinear Saint-Venant systems, where a deep operator network (DeepONet) learns the nominal backstepping control law and embeds it as prior knowledge into the actor and critic networks. A transfer-learning strategy preserves this prior during adaptation, improving learning efficiency and regulation performance over larger initial deviations compared to standard backstepping control.
AI.motivation: Backstepping control provides only local stability guarantees for nonlinear Saint-Venant systems, and its regulation performance degrades when operating far from the nominal equilibrium. This motivates combining model-based control knowledge with reinforcement learning to improve robustness and performance across a wider operating range.
AI.method: The nominal backstepping control law is learned using DeepONet and embedded as prior-informed feature representations into the actor and critic networks of a SAC framework. This learned prior is combined with the SAC policy to generate control inputs, and a transfer-learning strategy is used to preserve backstepping knowledge during adaptation to nonlinear dynamics.
AI.result: Simulation results on the Sambre River model show that the proposed method improves learning efficiency and maintains effective regulation over larger initial deviations than standard backstepping control.
AI.conclusion: The backstepping-guided SAC framework successfully integrates model-based control knowledge into RL, enhancing both learning efficiency and regulation performance for nonlinear Saint-Venant systems beyond the local validity region of backstepping control.

title: An AI-discovered smooth random fast dynamo on $\mathbb{T}^3$
summary: We construct a random, time-dependent divergence-free velocity field on $\mathbb{T}^3$---refreshing iid on finite time blocks and obeying deterministic $C^\infty_{t,x}$ bounds---that exhibits fast dynamo behavior. That is, for every fixed, sufficiently small resistivity, the almost sure exponential growth rate of the magnetic field solving the associated linear resistive induction equation is at least $1/2$; the exceptional null set may depend on the resistivity. We in fact get a time-uniform lower bound---with a random prefactor obeying a uniform-in-$κ$ inverse moment bound. The argument relies on a particular algebraic structure in Fourier space of the induction equation solution operator that allows us to propagate expected growth of the logarithmic size of three specially chosen Fourier modes. This allows us to reduce to a simple recursion, avoiding the complicated infinite-dimensional dynamics typical to the dynamo problem. The central proof idea was generated autonomously by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra; the manuscript was written (and verified) by the author.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a random, time-dependent divergence-free velocity field on the 3-torus that exhibits fast dynamo behavior: for any fixed sufficiently small resistivity, the magnetic field solving the linear resistive induction equation grows almost surely with exponential rate at least 1/2. The method uses a special algebraic structure in Fourier space to track three chosen Fourier modes via a simple recursion, avoiding infinite-dimensional dynamics.
AI.motivation: The dynamo problem—how a conductive fluid's motion amplifies magnetic fields—involves complicated infinite-dimensional dynamics. The authors aim to construct an explicit example of fast dynamo behavior (exponential magnetic field growth at small resistivity) that circumvents the typical analytical difficulties by exploiting algebraic structure in Fourier space.
AI.method: The velocity field is constructed stochastically, refreshing iid on finite time blocks while obeying deterministic C^∞ smoothness bounds. The key step is identifying an algebraic structure in the Fourier-space solution operator of the induction equation that lets the authors propagate expected growth of the logarithmic amplitude of three specially chosen Fourier modes. This reduces the problem to a simple recursion rather than tracking the full infinite-dimensional dynamics.
AI.result: For every fixed sufficiently small resistivity κ, the almost sure exponential growth rate of the magnetic field is at least 1/2 (the null set may depend on κ). A time-uniform lower bound is obtained with a random prefactor obeying a uniform-in-κ inverse moment bound.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous construction of a fast dynamo with a clean, reduced Fourier-mode recursion argument. Notably, the central proof idea was generated autonomously by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra, with the manuscript written and verified by the author.

title: The nested derivative criterion for determining elementary solutions to certain non-linear PDEs in one-dimensional space-time
summary: In this article, we have studied a particular criterion to establish if a particular class of nonlinear PDEs $\mathcal{O}_t u=\mathcal{O}_x u $ in unidimensional space-time $(x,t)$ admits elementary solutions respect to the spatial coordinate $x$, through the nested derivative method. Where a nested derivative is a generalization of the usual partial derivative of a order higher than one and, in terms of differentials operators, is a generalization of the Laguerre operator. This method integrated with Liouville's theorem and Galois theory e method by integrate by parts establish if solution of nested derivative equations admits elementary solutions respect with $x$. These solutions could help to study better evolutions of possible physical systems in space-time.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates a criterion for determining whether a class of nonlinear PDEs of the form O_t u = O_x u in one-dimensional space-time admits elementary solutions with respect to the spatial coordinate, using a nested derivative method (a generalization of higher-order partial derivatives and the Laguerre operator). The approach integrates Liouville's theorem, Galois theory, and integration by parts to establish when such solutions exist, potentially aiding the study of physical systems in space-time.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to develop a formal criterion for identifying whether nonlinear PDEs of a specific class admit elementary solutions with respect to the spatial variable, which could provide deeper insight into the evolution of physical systems in space-time.
AI.method: The method employs the nested derivative approach, which generalizes higher-order partial derivatives and the Laguerre operator. This is combined with Liouville's theorem, Galois theory, and integration by parts to establish criteria for the existence of elementary solutions in x.
AI.result: The paper establishes a criterion for determining when the given class of nonlinear PDEs admits elementary solutions with respect to the spatial coordinate x.
AI.conclusion: The nested derivative method, integrated with algebraic tools, provides a framework for determining elementary solvability of this PDE class, with potential applications to studying physical system evolution.

title: A note on interior curvature estimates for strictly convex solutions to the equation of prescribed curvature quotient
summary: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for strictly convex solutions to elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equations. The proof does not employ the advanced methods involving integral estimates or compactness arguments. Instead, it relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. Interior curvature estimates for strictly convex solutions to the special Lagrangian curvature equation in low dimensions also follow as a consequence.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a priori interior curvature bounds for strictly convex solutions to elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equations using an elementary maximum-principle argument with a novel auxiliary function, avoiding advanced integral or compactness techniques. Interior estimates for the special Lagrangian curvature equation in low dimensions follow as a corollary.
AI.motivation: The goal is to establish interior curvature estimates for strictly convex solutions to elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equations. The authors aim to provide a simpler proof that avoids the heavy machinery of integral estimates and compactness arguments typically used in such contexts.
AI.method: The proof uses a maximum-principle argument based on a concavity inequality for the equation operator, combined with a novel choice of an auxiliary function. This elementary approach circumvents the need for advanced integral estimates or compactness arguments.
AI.result: A priori interior curvature bounds are established for strictly convex solutions to elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equations. Additionally, interior curvature estimates for strictly convex solutions to the special Lagrangian curvature equation in low dimensions are obtained as a consequence.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that elementary maximum-principle techniques, together with a well-chosen auxiliary function and a concavity inequality, are sufficient to prove interior curvature bounds for these curvature equations, offering a more direct and accessible proof method than previously employed approaches.

title: On the closed solution of a problem coupling fluid infiltration with a hydration reaction
summary: We present a one-dimensional model for water infiltration coupled with a hydration reaction, relevant to coupled transport and chemical processes in the Earth's subsurface. In this model the sharp interface separating the saturated and dry regions evolves over time, leading to a moving free boundary problem. Consistent with recently presented numerical treatments in the literature, this solution indicates an interesting dynamic for the free boundary. At early time, for a given domain porosity, the infiltration front advances with a specific square-root-in-time behavior. At later time, depending on the consumption of the hydration reaction, the front advance can exhibit square-root, linear, or exponential forms. The presented closed solution provides an analytical tool that can be used to quantify important behavior in coupled transport and reaction systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a one-dimensional analytical model for water infiltration coupled with a hydration reaction, formulated as a moving free boundary problem. The closed-form solution reveals that the infiltration front advances with square-root-in-time behavior at early times, and can exhibit square-root, linear, or exponential front advance at later times depending on the hydration reaction consumption rate.
AI.motivation: To provide an analytical tool for quantifying coupled transport and chemical processes in the Earth's subsurface, complementing existing numerical treatments that have observed interesting free boundary dynamics but lack closed-form solutions.
AI.method: A one-dimensional model of water infiltration coupled with a hydration reaction is formulated as a moving free boundary problem, where the sharp interface between saturated and dry regions evolves over time. A closed-form analytical solution is derived for this system.
AI.result: The solution shows that at early times the infiltration front advances with a square-root-in-time behavior (for given porosity). At later times, depending on hydration reaction consumption, the front advance can take square-root, linear, or exponential forms.
AI.conclusion: The closed-form solution provides a quantitative analytical framework for understanding coupled transport and reaction systems in subsurface environments, consistent with previously reported numerical results.

title: Boundary layers and vanishing diffusivity in run-and-tumble models
summary: A notable feature of confined active matter systems is the tendency for motile particles to accumulate near solid boundaries. In various linear models with no-flux boundary conditions, this accumulation is realized through the development of sharp boundary layers at small particle diffusivity $κ$. In this paper, we present the first rigorous investigation of nonlinear boundary layers in the context of confined active matter. Specifically, we consider a family of 1D run-and-tumble models with nonlinear advection and tumbling on the half-line $\mathbb{R}_+$. We rigorously prove the vanishing diffusivity limit with quantitative convergence rates. In the limiting system, the boundary mass enters as a new variable which solves a nonlinear ODE, coupled to the PDE through a dynamic boundary condition. Interestingly, the nonlinearity on the boundary at $κ= 0$ cannot be obtained without reference to the boundary layer analysis at $κ\ll 1$. Numerically, these models exhibit rich behavior, including phase transition and hysteresis in the boundary layer.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first rigorous mathematical analysis of nonlinear boundary layers in confined active matter systems. Using 1D run-and-tumble models with nonlinear advection and tumbling on the half-line, the authors prove the vanishing diffusivity limit with quantitative convergence rates, showing that boundary mass emerges as a new variable solving a nonlinear ODE coupled to the PDE via a dynamic boundary condition.
AI.motivation: Confined active matter systems exhibit particle accumulation near boundaries, traditionally studied through linear models showing sharp boundary layers at small diffusivity. A rigorous mathematical investigation of nonlinear boundary layers in this context was previously lacking.
AI.method: The authors study a family of 1D run-and-tumble models with nonlinear advection and tumbling on the half-line, and rigorously prove the vanishing diffusivity limit with quantitative convergence rates using boundary layer analysis.
AI.result: The vanishing diffusivity limit is proven rigorously with quantitative convergence rates. In the limit, boundary mass appears as a new variable governed by a nonlinear ODE coupled to the PDE through a dynamic boundary condition. The nonlinear boundary condition at κ=0 depends intrinsically on the boundary layer analysis at small κ. Numerical simulations reveal phase transitions and hysteresis in the boundary layer.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the first rigorous treatment of nonlinear boundary layers in confined active matter, revealing that the effective boundary dynamics at zero diffusivity cannot be derived without understanding the boundary layer structure at small diffusivity, and that such systems support rich phenomena including phase transitions and hysteresis.

title: Optimal regularity of stable harmonic maps to spheres
summary: In this paper, we show that the codimension of the singular set of a stable stationary harmonic map to a round $k$-sphere is at least $k+1$ when $k$ is between 3 and 6, and is at least 7 when $k$ is at least 7. The result is sharp in the sense that there exist energy minimizing 0-homogeneous maps in the aforementioned critical dimensions. We also establish non-trivial index bounds for the non-constant harmonic maps from $n$-spheres to $k$-spheres, provided that $n$ is less than $k$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves sharp lower bounds on the codimension of the singular set for stable stationary harmonic maps into round k-spheres, showing the codimension is at least k+1 for 3≤k≤6 and at least 7 for k≥7. The bounds are sharp, as demonstrated by energy-minimizing 0-homogeneous maps. Additionally, the paper establishes nontrivial index bounds for non-constant harmonic maps from n-spheres to k-spheres when n<k.
AI.motivation: To determine the optimal regularity (singular set dimension) of stable stationary harmonic maps into spheres, which is a fundamental question in geometric measure theory and calculus of variations.
AI.method: The paper uses techniques from geometric measure theory and harmonic map analysis to analyze the singular set structure, combined with explicit constructions of 0-homogeneous energy-minimizing maps to establish sharpness, and employs Morse index theory for the index bounds.
AI.result: Codimension of the singular set of stable stationary harmonic maps to S^k is at least k+1 for 3≤k≤6 and at least 7 for k≥7; sharp bounds confirmed by explicit examples; nontrivial index bounds for harmonic maps from S^n to S^k with n<k.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes sharp regularity results for stable stationary harmonic maps into spheres and provides new index bounds connecting the topology of the domain and target spheres to the Morse index of harmonic maps.

title: A two-point phase recovering with spherical wave reference
summary: We consider a reference wave, a radiation solution, and the sum of these solutions (total solution) for the Helmholtz equation in an exterior region. We give two-point formulas for approximate phase recovering of the radiation solution from the intensity of the total solution for the case of spherical reference wave. We show that these formulas can be used, in particular, for approximate phase recovering from holographic data on a single plane. By these formulas, we continue previous studies with plane wave reference.

AI.tldr: The paper presents two-point formulas for approximate phase recovery of a radiation solution from intensity measurements of a total solution (reference wave + radiation solution) for the Helmholtz equation, specifically using a spherical reference wave. These formulas enable approximate phase recovery from holographic data on a single plane, extending prior work that used plane wave references.

title: Uniform large deviation principles for the stochastic heat equation over unbounded sets of initial data
summary: We study small-noise large deviations for the stochastic heat equation (SHE) on the torus with unbounded, multiplicative space-time white noise. We establish uniform large deviation principles (ULDPs) over unbounded sets of initial data, alongside novel well-posedness and regularity results. The ULDPs are obtained for both continuous-in-space and $L^p$ initial data. For these two classes, the ULDP holds uniformly over $L^q$-bounded subsets, with $q<\infty$ and $q<p$ allowed respectively, so these sets are highly unbounded in the state space. The admissible range of $q$ is dictated by the growth of the noise coefficient in the SHE. Crucially, our methods allow us to reach down to $q=1$. This yields ULDPs over $L^1$-bounded subsets, enabling the study of exit times in physical systems with mass conservation.

The ULDPs hold uniformly over L^q-bounded subsets with remarkably broad (down to q=1) ranges, enabling applications to physical systems with mass conservation.

Previous results were restricted to bounded sets, which limits applicability to physical systems such as mass-conserving models where L^1-bounded initial data naturally arise.

The methods are designed to reach down to q=1, which is the critical case for physical applications.

For continuous initial data, the ULDP holds uniformly over L^q-bounded subsets for any q<∞; for L^p initial data, it holds uniformly over L^q-bounded subsets with q<p. The admissible range of q is determined by the growth of the noise coefficient, and the methods achieve the optimal case q=1.

title: Necessary conditions for deterministic and stochastic maximal regularity
summary:
We study the role of Banach space geometry in deterministic and stochastic maximal regularity. We first construct an example showing that the UMD assumption in Weis' characterisation of maximal $L^p$-regularity in terms of $R$-sectoriality cannot be omitted. Combining this construction with an equivalence between stochastic maximal regularity and deterministic maximal regularity on the $2$-concavification of the underlying space, we obtain an operator on a UMD Banach function space of type $2$ that has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus of angle zero, but fails stochastic maximal $L^p$-regularity (SMR$_p$) for every $p\in[2,\infty)$.
  Motivated by this example, we study the Banach space geometry hypothesis underlying SMR$_p$ more closely. This is an $R$-boundedness condition $(S_p)$ for stochastic convolution operators. For UMD spaces $X$ of type $2$, we show that this condition is not only sufficient, but also necessary for two canonical test operators: a diagonal multiplier on a Rademacher space and, for $q>2$, the Laplacian on $L^q(\mathbb R^d;X)$. Finally, we prove that its interval-kernel and exponential-kernel formulations are equivalent and that, at the endpoint $p=2$, condition $(S_2)$ holds if and only if $X$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space.

AI.tldr: This paper examines the role of Banach space geometry in deterministic and stochastic maximal regularity, constructing counterexamples and establishing necessary and sufficient conditions linking R-boundedness, UMD spaces, and stochastic maximal L^p-regularity.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand which Banach space geometric assumptions are truly necessary (not just sufficient) for stochastic maximal L^p-regularity, particularly questioning whether the UMD assumption in Weis' characterization of maximal L^p-regularity can be relaxed, and whether condition (S_p) is essential.
AI.method: The paper constructs a counterexample showing UMD cannot be omitted in Weis' characterization, then uses an equivalence between stochastic and deterministic maximal regularity on the 2-concavification to build an operator with a bounded H^∞-calculus of angle zero on a type 2 UMD space that still fails SMR_p. They then analyze the R-boundedness condition (S_p) for stochastic convolution operators, showing it is necessary for two canonical test operators, and prove equivalence of interval-kernel and exponential-kernel formulations, including a Hilbert space characterization at p=2.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates: (1) UMD cannot be omitted in Weis' characterization; (2) there exists an operator on a type 2 UMD Banach function space with bounded H^∞-calculus of angle zero that fails SMR_p for all p∈[2,∞); (3) condition (S_p) is necessary for canonical test operators (diagonal multiplier on Rademacher space and Laplacian on L^q(ℝ^d;X)); (4) interval-kernel and exponential-kernel formulations of (S_p) are equivalent; (5) at p=2, condition (S_2) characterizes Hilbert spaces up to isomorphism.
AI.conclusion: The paper clarifies the precise geometric assumptions needed for stochastic maximal regularity, showing that the R-boundedness condition (S_p) is both necessary and sufficient for key test operators, and that the endpoint case p=2 fundamentally characterizes Hilbert spaces.

title: Complete Symbols of Equivariant Pseudodifferential Operators on Noncompact Symmetric Spaces
summary: We study $G$-equivariant Hörmander pseudodifferential operators on a noncompact symmetric space $G/K$. We define a notion of a complete symbol function, called the Harish-Chandra symbol function, on the spherical tempered dual of $G$, for operators that satisfy a rapid off-diagonal decay condition on their Schwartz kernels, and we characterize the class of such operators in terms of their Harish-Chandra symbol function.

AI.conclusion: The Harish-Chandra symbol function provides a complete framework for characterizing a natural class of equivariant pseudodifferential operators on noncompact symmetric spaces.
